Pilot design details such as universal eligibility mechanics, procurement rules, and staffing provisions are unspecified.

sociology_baseline.note: Moderate persuasion range; stakeholders can shift within practical cost-benefit bounds.
Visible budget overruns or service failures could push moderate observers into active participation.
Many affected individuals are unlikely to speak publicly unless issues become salient.
Stakeholders are likely to cluster discussion within role-based communities.
Broader opinion shifts likely require repeated confirming signals, not a single message.
Role identities shape interpretation of the pilot's success criteria.
General public attention is likely to fade without controversy or new evidence.

sociology_prompt_influences.description: Frames emphasizing child wellbeing and reduced stigma may increase support among parents and general observers.
Cost-growth narratives may disproportionately activate fiscally cautious parents and political leadership.
Reports of cafeteria overload may reduce political durability unless paired with mitigation steps.
Evidence of local farm participation may improve legitimacy if not associated with excessive price increases.
